extracted.intended_audience: life-science authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors
extracted.subtask_description: Describing the aims and operational standards of a platform that provides journal-independent peer review for life-science manuscripts and produces Refereed Preprints to streamline submission to journals. Covers what is delivered to authors and how the service interfaces with preprint servers and affiliate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality journal-independent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons is a platform for high-quality journal-independent peer review in the life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioning: peer review performed independently of any single journal to focus on scientific quality rather than journal-specific fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereed Preprint composition (manuscript, reports, authors' response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide authors with a Refereed Preprint, which includes the authors’ manuscript, reports from a single round of peer review and the authors’ response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliverable requirement: the Refereed Preprint must contain the manuscript plus the peer-review reports from one review round and the authors' formal response, so that the package documents the review exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single round of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports from a single round of peer review are included in the Refereed Preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process constraint: Review Commons emphasizes producing a single round of referee reports (rather than multiple serial re-reviews) to create a stable, citable refereed preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate author-directed submission to affiliate journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons facilitates author-directed submission of Refereed Preprints to affiliate journals to expedite editorial consideration, reduce serial re-review and streamline publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service expectation: the platform supports authors in submitting the refereed preprint to participating journals to speed editorial evaluation and reduce repeated peer review at multiple journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability to bioRxiv and affiliate journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons transfers Refereed Preprints on behalf of the authors to bioRxiv and 28 affiliate journals from EMBO Press, eLife, ASCB, The Company of Biologists, Rockefeller University Press, PLOS, the Biochemical Society and FEBS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interoperability requirement: the Refereed Preprint must be in a form and accompanied by materials that Review Commons can forward to bioRxiv and listed affiliate journals to enable streamlined onward submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers focus on science, not journal fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow reviewers to focus on the science, not specific journal fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation principle: reviewer responsibilities and report framing should prioritise scientific validity, rigor, and significance rather than advising on whether the work is suited to a particular journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrich preprints, reduce re-review, and accelerate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons will enrich the value of preprints, reduce re-reviewing at multiple journals, and accelerate the publishing process by providing journals with high-quality referee reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome goals: the platform aims for the Refereed Preprint and its reports to add measurable value to preprints, lower redundant reviewing across journals, and shorten time-to-decision by supplying journals with thorough referee reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author empowerment and agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons empowers authors by providing them with a Refereed Preprint and facilitating its submission to affiliate journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User-centered principle: authors retain control over submission direction while gaining a documented, peer-reviewed package to support editorial consideration.
